en.text: The mother is in the garden.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: The → mother → is → in → the → garden
grammarExplanation: English uses 'is' for location.
The place phrase tells where the person is.
German keeps the finite verb in second position.
Location phrases often use dative forms such as im, am, or in der.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: La → madre → está → en → el → jardín
grammarExplanation: Spanish uses estar for location.

en.text: The grandmother sits near the chair.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: The → grandmother → sits → near → the → chair
grammarExplanation: English places the verb after the subject.
The object receives the action.

de.text: Die Großmutter sitzt neben dem Stuhl.

grammarExplanation: German uses verb-second word order.

fr.text: La grand-mère est assise près de la chaise.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: La → grand-mère → est → assise → près → de → la → chaise
grammarExplanation: French usually places the verb after the subject.
Articles and contractions must match the noun.

es.text: La abuela se sienta cerca de la silla.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: La → abuela → se → sienta → cerca → de → la → silla
grammarExplanation: Spanish verbs agree with the subject.
